title: What could break this
body:
The Sivers bull case rests on a sequence: two production ramps both hit their 2026 targets, a $453M pipeline converts to revenue faster than dilution compounds, and a US Nasdaq listing unlocks the capital needed to cross operating breakeven. Disrupt any single link — and the timeline for profitability, already not arriving before 2027 in the analyst base case, slides into 2028 or beyond. Below are the specific failure modes, grounded in disclosed facts.

## The calendar problem

Both of Sivers' highest-stakes production milestones fall within a seven-to-nine month window from the snapshot date. The POET Technologies collaboration, [announced September 29, 2025](https://www.sivers-semiconductors.com/), targets production-readiness for its External Light Source modules by end-2026. The unnamed automotive LiDAR customer — disclosed in analyst research as a strategic partner incorporating Sivers technology "across all their platforms" — is targeting a Q4 2026 production ramp with lifecycle revenue estimated at $53–138M over an eight-to-ten year period, representing 16–44% of FY2025 sales.

Semiconductor production ramps do not routinely hit first-announced dates. Yield qualification, component supply chain alignment, and customer qualification testing each add latency that compounds. A two-quarter slip in either program would not merely delay revenue recognition; it would compress the operating margin improvement trajectory that underpins consensus for a 2027 EBIT crossover. With operating margin running at -39% in FY2025 — itself an improvement from -83% in 2022 — there is no buffer. The company has demonstrated directional improvement; it has not demonstrated an ability to execute a simultaneous dual production ramp.

## The runway equation

At year-end 2025, Sivers held SEK 43.5M in cash against free cash flow of approximately -SEK 66M in the fiscal year. The gap was bridged in February 2026 with a $17M term loan and convertible, followed by a $6.6M non-dilutive NEMC grant in May. Each injection extends the runway; none resolves the structural equation.

Since 2020, shares outstanding have grown by 101.58% — the company has roughly doubled its share count to stay operational through the pre-profitability phase. The June 15 AGM includes authorization for management to issue up to a further 15% of shares without a full rights process. That headroom request is not neutral: boards seek dilution authority because they expect to use it. A continued equity tap running in parallel with a planned Nasdaq listing simultaneously increases the float available to US investors and further erodes the per-share value of existing Swedish holders' positions.

## A pipeline is not a backlog

The $453M contract pipeline — up 64% year-on-year — is the most-cited metric in the Sivers investment narrative. It deserves scrutiny. The named counterparties driving that figure are POET, Ayar Labs, O-Net/Enablence, and the automotive LiDAR strategic customer. Each represents a multi-quarter design win, not a purchase order. The automotive customer alone accounts for $53–138M of estimated lifecycle value across 8–10 years.

Design wins can be withdrawn. A customer may pivot to a competing laser supplier, delay platform launch, or restructure supply chain before production commences. The automotive customer — the single largest disclosed lifecycle exposure — has not yet entered production ramp. If that program were to exit before volumes begin, the pipeline headline would fall materially, and with it the 7.2x forward price-to-sales multiple that current shareholders have priced in. The $453M number is a probability-weighted projection over a decade-long horizon, not recognised revenue. No conversion rate has yet been established by results.

## The chokepoint is closing

The strategic logic of the Sivers pure-play thesis depends on large integrated players not replicating its InP DFB laser capacity quickly enough to displace it from new design wins. That assumption is under active pressure. Coherent (COHR) doubled its InP wafer output capacity one quarter ahead of its own schedule, per the company's FY2026 disclosures. Lumentum (LITE) acquired a fifth InP fabrication facility. Most consequentially, NVIDIA committed $2 billion each to COHR and LITE in March 2026 — capital injections explicitly targeting the optical component capacity bottleneck that defines Sivers' position.

These are not peripheral competitors. They are vertically integrated players with wafer-to-module manufacturing and established hyperscaler relationships. If their capacity expansions close the chokepoint before Sivers completes its production ramp and locks in the next generation of design wins, Sivers' pricing leverage and design-win capture rate both weaken simultaneously.

## What the restatement signals

The PCAOB-aligned restatement disclosed in May 2026 widened the FY2025 EBIT loss by SEK 36M, moving the reported figure from -SEK 141M to -SEK 178M. The FY2024 comparative was also revised: revenue fell from SEK 243.7M to SEK 219.2M while the net loss widened from SEK 116.3M to SEK 183.9M. Identified drivers include impairment of previously capitalised development expenditures, inventory revaluation, revenue reallocation across periods, and revised share-based compensation fair values — a pattern consistent with Swedish K3 accounting applying more aggressive recognition timing than US GAAP permits.

| Period | Net Sales (K3, SEK M) | Net Sales (PCAOB, SEK M) | Net Result (K3, SEK M) | Net Result (PCAOB, SEK M) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| FY2024 | 243.7 | 219.2 | -116.3 | -183.9 |
| FY2025 | 304.1 | 306.6 | -186.5 | -222.6 |

The question for prospective Nasdaq investors is whether this restatement is bounded. The dual-listing audit is ongoing. If further PCAOB review surfaces additional adjustments — particularly in revenue recognition or R&D capitalisation — the listing could be delayed or downsized, and the SEK 72.90 share price, which rallied sharply on listing anticipation, would correct against the downward-revised historical numbers.

## The overhang that stays

Co-founder Erik Fällström departs the board at the June 15 AGM, but his economic stake — approximately 11.8% of votes via DDM Debt and the Fällström Family Office — remains intact. DDM has publicly stated it wants to drive Sivers toward a "broader investment company," a direction incompatible with the focused operating-company narrative that a US institutional roadshow requires. His removal from governance eliminates one source of strategic friction; his continued shareholding preserves the optionality to reassert it through other means, including a push for strategic alternatives or a recapitalisation on different terms.

Simultaneously, Sweden's Economic Crime Authority (Ekobrottsmyndigheten) is investigating market abuse related to the Nasdaq listing announcement, which leaked approximately 48 hours early via an anonymous X account. An adverse finding would not impair operations, but it would feature in the listing prospectus and give US institutional investors — who operate their own compliance gatekeepers — a documented reason to pass.

Finally, the currency exposure is structural rather than hedgeable at Sivers' current scale. Q4 2025 revenue grew 5% as reported but 17% in constant FX terms — a 12-percentage-point gap driven by SEK appreciation. Sustained SEK strength compresses reported revenue against a dollar-denominated cost of capital that US investors will use to judge the company. A company pitching a Nasdaq listing on Swedish-crown-reported numbers is asking investors to build their own FX model, and few will bother.
